subject: Observability: per-deployment telemetry, anomaly detection & exception workflow
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Product Team <product@redwood.com>, Eng Observability <eng-observability@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability: per-deployment telemetry, anomaly detection & exception workflow

Team —

Quick ask coming out of a renewal prep with Acme Cloud (Karen Liu). They want: per-deployment (hosted/dedicated/private) cost & median/tail-latency slices by route, lightweight anomaly detection that surfaces when a route's cost-per-token or p95 moves by >20% week-over-week, and a clearly visible exception workflow (who to page / fallback models / suggested rollback).

Current console gives per-route summaries, but customers are asking for:
- a per-deployment dimension (we need to show the same route across hosted vs dedicated pools)
- automatic anomaly flags with simple root-cause hints (high GPU utilization, quantization downgrade, sudden input-size shift)
- an actionable exception panel that ties directly to rollout policies (can trigger fallback to a cheaper model with a button)

Can eng-observability and product sync on what we can realistically ship in the next quarter vs a roadmap spike? Monica — putting you on notice since CS will need messaging/playbooks. I attached a CSV with sample event slices from Acme for context.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference

Attachments: example_query.csv (CSV sample of route events), screenshot-console-proto.png (low-fidelity mock)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Eng Observability <eng-observability@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability: per-deployment telemetry, anomaly detection & exception workflow

Thanks for the context, Irene — this is exactly the type of ask we've been hearing from a few strategic accounts. A couple of clarifying questions before I propose prioritization:

1) For "per-deployment", do they require cross-deployment aggregation (i.e., show a single route aggregated across hosted/dedicated/private) or separate tabs per deployment?
2) For anomaly detection, is the expectation that we run detection server-side and attach flags to existing route rows, or provide an analyst UI (time-series explorer) where CS can run detections on demand?
3) For the exception workflow, rules vs manual triggers — should we expose a single-click fallback tied to the rollout config, or only surface recommended steps with links to the rollout page?

My initial thought: scope a 6-sprint (3-month) piece for a basic per-deployment dimension + simple server-side anomaly flags (20% delta detection) with a "Suggested Action" dropdown. Add a follow-up spike for a one-click fallback that wires into rollout config.

If engineering agrees, I'll sketch a PRD and priority bucket. Monica — can you draft the CS playbook outline so we have required content for the PRD?

-Laura
Product Manager, Console & Observability

--

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Eng Observability <eng-observability@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability: per-deployment telemetry, anomaly detection & exception workflow

High-level feasibility from the observability squad:

- Per-deployment dimension: straightforward on the query layer if we tag every request with deployment_id (hosted/dedicated/private + pool id). We already emit deployment metadata for telemetry; the work is indexing and adding the UI dimension. Estimated: 3-4 sprints for proto (backend + UI table + filters).

- Server-side anomaly detection: we can implement a simple rule-based detector (percent-change over fixed window) with very low infra cost. ML-based detectors are higher effort (~6-8 sprints). Suggested phased approach:
  Phase 1: rule-based flags (20% delta w/ configurable baseline window), show "likely cause" by mapping correlated signals (GPU util higher than usual, input-length shift >30%, quantization level changed). (2 sprints)
  Phase 2: optional ML anomaly runner for noisy routes (4-6 sprints).

- Actionable exception panel: this is the trickiest. We need the rollout API to be able to accept a programmatic fallback trigger. Today's rollout service supports manual rollback via the console, but there is no one-click API for fallbacks. Adding a protected API + audit trail is another 3 sprints (backend + RBAC). UI wiring + confirmation flows + PD integration ~2 sprints.

Risk notes: high-cardinality routes (per-customer route variants) will blow up query cost. We should add sampling and capped cardinality in the proto. CSV attached looks good; it confirms heavy tail for Acme's per-customer route variants.

Proposal: allocate a 2-week spike to implement a read-only prototype for per-deployment filters and rule-based flags (no rollback button yet). If that works, follow with a 6-sprint roadmap for the rest. Who owns the spike?

-dylan
Lead SWE, Observability

--

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability: per-deployment telemetry, anomaly detection & exception workflow

Irene / Laura — draft CS playbook attached in-line below (short form). I took a look at the CSV and mocked the messaging we'd need during renewal conversations.

Playbook (short):
- When anomaly flag appears: create internal incident (link to console row) + run quick checks (Is the customer pinned to a dedicated pool? Any recent rollout changes in last 24h?)
- Suggested first actions: escalate to SRE if GPU util > 80%, toggle fallback to last-stable model if p95 > threshold and fallback API exists, or submit rollback request via rollout console link.
- Customer-facing wording: acknowledge, share ETA for investigation (2h triage), and provide temporary mitigations (scale up pool or enable caching).

I can expand this into a full template once product confirms the UI/flags shape. Happy to own customer messaging and templates.

-Monica
Senior Customer Success Manager

--

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karen Liu <karen.liu@acmecloud.com>, Andy Park <andy.park@evex.io>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability: per-deployment telemetry, anomaly detection & exception workflow

Thanks all — that plan sounds sensible and aligns with Acme's asks. Two quick decisions so we can move forward:

1) Spike owner: Dylan, can your team take the 2-week read-only spike to produce a prototype filter + server-side 20% rule-based flag? Please include a lightweight sample dashboard for Acme to review.

2) CS deliverable: Monica, please prepare the customer playbook + an "investigate" checklist that maps to the signals Dylan called out. If possible, include templated customer wording for renewals.

Laura — please go ahead and draft the PRD with the phased milestones (spike -> proto -> rollback API). If we can commit the spike for the week of Nov 30, I will tell Acme we can share a prototype the following week.

Karen/Andy — thanks for flagging this; we'll share the prototype link and get your feedback on whether the anomaly rules catch the patterns in the attached CSV.

Irene
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
